hook.text: Early cars used gas lamps that flickered in the wind. Modern headlights see farther than you can.

buildup.text: Halogen bulbs dominated for decades—cheap, warm, but not very bright or energy-efficient.

discovery.text: Xenon (HID) lights were three times brighter. LEDs then offered that brightness with far less power.

twist.text: Laser headlights can illuminate 600 meters ahead—twice the range of LEDs.

climax.text: Adaptive headlights use cameras to dim individual pixels, keeping beams on without blinding others.

punchline.text: Car lights evolved from candles to cameras.

quiz.question: What can adaptive headlights do?
options: Dim pixels to avoid blinding others
